tagline: Up the St. Croix from the Mississippi into the North Country.
intro: From Point Douglas, where the St. Croix runs into the Mississippi, the byway follows the valley north for 124 miles to a point past Sandstone. The south end is long views over rolling ground. Farther north it turns to rock, cliffs and woods, and by Pine County, as the state tourism office puts it, you have truly arrived in the North Country.
The river is one of the eight original National Wild and Scenic Rivers. Point Douglas had a mill, warehouses and a lime kiln in 1856. What is left of it now is a small development along US 10.

moments.title: Stillwater
moments.text: Named in 1843 for the calm of the river by the man who built its first sawmill, Stillwater held the 1848 convention that started Minnesota toward statehood.

moments.title: Interstate State Park
moments.text: At Taylors Falls the river squeezes through the Dalles, a deep basalt gorge full of glacial potholes, and in 1886 a log jam here was a tourist attraction in its own right.

moments.title: Hinckley
moments.text: A firestorm wiped out Hinckley on September 1, 1894, and the depot rebuilt on the same spot afterward now houses the Hinckley Fire Museum.
